papers.title: Widespread endocrine-disrupting pollutant alters male courtship behavior in a livebearing fish.
papers.journal: Behavioral ecology : official journal of the International Society for Behavioral Ecology
papers.abstract: Sexual selection is a potent evolutionary force shaping both precopulatory courtship behavior and postcopulatory sperm traits, with male reproductive effort often adjusted to social and mating context. Endocrine-disrupting contaminants are predicted to alter how males allocate reproductive effort, yet their behavioral effects across different mating contexts remain poorly understood. We examined whether exposure to 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2; 43 to 1,100 ng/L), a synthetic estrogen used in the contraceptive pill that enters aquatic systems via wastewater effluent, alters male courtship behavior and sperm traits in a freshwater fish (Dermogenys collettei). Using assays in which males encountered females either sequentially or simultaneously, we quantified courtship behavior and latency to interact, alongside sperm viability, morphology, and performance. Exposure to high EE2 consistently reduced male mating effort. Exposed males were slower to initiate interactions with females and expressed less courtship behavior in both sequential and simultaneous assays. In contrast, EE2 had no detectable effects on sperm traits, and male preferences for female gravid spot size were unaffected. These findings suggest estrogenic pollution can disproportionately reduce mating effort, revealing a decoupling between behavioral and postcopulatory responses.

papers.title: Exploring sexuality, sexual well-being and intimacy in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: systematic review and meta-synthesis of qualitative studies.
papers.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sexuality and intimacy are central dimensions of identity, emotional well-being, social connectedness, and quality of life. In individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs), these domains may be profoundly affected by illness-related, psychological, interpersonal, social, institutional, and treatment-related factors. Although antipsychotic-induced sexual dysfunction is clinically relevant, a broader understanding of patients' subjective experiences is needed to capture the meaning of sexuality, intimacy, and relational well-being in this population. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the ENTREQ framework. PubMed, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched to identify qualitative and mixed-methods studies exploring patients' subjective experiences of sexuality, sexual well-being, intimate relationships, and antipsychotic-induced sexual dysfunction in SSDs. RESULTS: Fifteen reports from 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. Thematic synthesis identified six overarching descriptive themes: (1) illness-related challenges to sexual well-being, (2) abuse and traumatic experiences, (3) beliefs about sexuality, (4) the role of the healthcare system, (5) barriers and facilitators of sexual well-being, and (6) antipsychotic-induced sexual side effects. Patients' accounts showed that sexuality was not limited to sexual functioning, but was closely connected to self-image, stigma, emotional closeness, relational opportunities, trauma, institutional restrictions, and communication with clinicians. The analytical synthesis indicated that these factors interacted through their effects on self-image, relational confidence, opportunities for intimacy, and sexual agency, potentially reinforcing vulnerability or supporting well-being and personal recovery. papers.title: Creative thinking in humans and artificial intelligence: A comparative review of neural, molecular, and social mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Creative thinking drives the generation of novel and useful ideas, contributing to scientific progress and the resolution of social challenges. Evidence from the earliest stone tools, dating to approximately 3.3 million years ago, suggests that creativity among hominin ancestors played a key role in the emergence of human culture and civilization. Although creativity arises from brain activity, the underlying molecular mechanisms and neural substrates remain incompletely understood. Neurotransmitters involved in motivation, reward, and mood play crucial roles in promoting creative processes. Recent advances in high-resolution brain imaging have begun to identify both specific brain regions and large-scale neural networks associated with creative thinking. Meanwhile, rapid developments in artificial intelligence (AI) raise questions about whether machines can exhibit forms of creativity once considered uniquely human. The integration of large language models, multimodal learning, and next-generation computing technologies, including quantum computing, may substantially expand the capabilities of AI systems. Simultaneously, these technological advances are generating new insights and discussions about the characteristics and limitations of human intellectual activity, thereby underscoring the importance of creativity. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular, neural, and social dimensions of creative thinking, compares the underlying characteristics of human and artificial creativity, and discusses how interactions between biological and AI may shape the future of creativity in the era of human-AI coexistence.

papers.title: Testosterone and cortisol distributions reveal men's relationship status: Evidence from a study with daily hormone sampling.
papers.abstract: Prior studies support men in romantic relationships having lower testosterone and cortisol concentrations than single men. Such studies have generally collected only 1-2 hormone samples per participant, which has left unknown how hormone values are distributed within individuals and whether differences in such distributions can be used to accurately classify men by their relationship status. We collected daily measures of testosterone and cortisol across 31 days from each of 41 young men (N = 1143 observations). Signal detection analyses demonstrated good discrimination of relationship status from subject-mean hormone concentrations. Furthermore, the daily sampling revealed a novel pattern: partnered men almost never experienced high testosterone or high cortisol days. Additional analyses supported replication of prior findings showing positive associations between sociosexual desires and testosterone concentrations among partnered men. These findings are consistent with theoretical models that propose hormonal mediation of tradeoffs between men's mating effort and investment in committed relationships.

papers.title: Apologising in Saudi Arabic: A sociopragmatic analysis.
papers.abstract: This study describes how Saudi Arabic speakers apologise across socially varied situations. A written discourse completion task was completed by 102 male Saudi undergraduates. It yielded 811 responses to eight scenarios differing in social distance, power relationship, and severity of offence. Responses were coded for the five apology strategies of the CCSARP tradition. Because the scenarios vary in several respects at once, the study compares apology behaviour across situation types rather than isolating single variables. Saudi apologies emerged as elaborate, multi-move acts anchored in the explicit apology formula. Most responses combined an apology expression with an explanation, and over half offered repair. Overt acknowledgement of responsibility appeared in under a quarter of responses, and promises of forbearance were rare. Two situational patterns stood out. Offers of repair clustered in the close-relationship scenarios. Overt responsibility acknowledgement was largely confined to the two scenarios in which the speaker apologises for prior rudeness towards a service worker. Explanations were most frequent in apologies to superiors, and no forbearance promises occurred for minor offences. The analysis is framed through rapport management, Culpeper's impoliteness work, and Saudi-grounded face research. It documents culture-specific formulae, including oath intensifiers and the relational formula ḥaqqak 'alayya, through which responsibility and reassurance are made culturally legible.

papers.title: Molecularly Anchored n-Type Quinone/Graphene Heterostructures Enabling High-Capacity and Ultra-stable Proton Storage.
papers.abstract: Quinone-based organic electrodes are attractive for aqueous proton batteries owing to their fast and reversible proton-coupled redox chemistry. However, their practical application is largely restricted by severe dissolution in acidic electrolytes, poor structural stability, and low electronic conductivity. Herein, we report a molecularly anchored n-type quinone/graphene heterostructure constructed by integrating tetraaminobenzoquinone (TABq) with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) through a facile solvothermal strategy. Strong π-π stacking, hydrogen-bonding interactions, and covalent linkages effectively immobilize TABq molecules on the conductive rGO framework, thereby suppressing active-material dissolution, enhancing electrode integrity, and constructing efficient electron/proton transport pathways. The open heterointerface and abundant redox-active sites further promote rapid proton uptake/release and accelerate charge-transfer kinetics. Benefiting from this rational heterostructure design, the optimized TABq/rGO electrode delivers a high specific capacity of 349.78 mAh g-1 at 1 A g-1, remarkable rate capability of 131.12 mAh g-1 even at 100 A g-1, and excellent cycling durability. When coupled with a 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride anode, the full cell achieves a reversible capacity of 129.03 mAh g-1 at 0.75 A g-1 and maintains 75.43% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Moreover, TABq/rGO-based symmetric proton battery exhibits outstanding long-term stability, retaining 74.17% of its capacity after 10,000 cycles. Experimental characterizations combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that the TABq/rGO heterointerface regulates charge distribution, stabilizes the quinone redox centers, and lowers the kinetic barrier for proton storage. This work highlights an effective molecular anchoring strategy for developing high-capacity, high-rate, and durable organic electrodes for advanced aqueous proton batteries.

papers.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum-Ion Batteries via Weak-Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Aqueous aluminum-ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak-coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)3), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al3+, displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO-mediated solvation disruption with FEC-enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel-to-layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g-1. By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

papers.title: Hybridization-Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor-Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation.
papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell-selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP-ssDNA) along the target region of single-guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP-ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP-ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor-selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9-encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP-ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor-bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS-STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

papers.title: Self-Powered Multivariable Organic Photovoltaic Sensors for Accurate Volatile Organic Compound Discrimination.
papers.abstract: Most existing VOC sensors rely on battery power and only single-parameter outputs, limiting long-term deployment, maintenance efficiency, and chemical discrimination. Here, we report a self-powered multivariable photovoltaic sensor (MPVS) that repurposes an organic photovoltaic junction as an information-rich VOC sensing platform. By integrating a gas-permeable silver nanowire electrode with a donor-acceptor bulk-heterojunction active layer, the MPVS enables efficient analyte access while maintaining stable photovoltaic operation under illumination. Exposure to VOCs induces coupled and reversible changes in open-circuit voltage (VOC) and short-circuit current density (JSC), providing two orthogonal sensing features without external power input. Using a single PM6:Y6 junction, we demonstrate concentration-dependent responses and reliable discrimination of representative VOCs. Extending the concept to a five-element MPVS array incorporating different Y-series acceptors generates high-dimensional photovoltaic fingerprints that enable accurate identification of eight chemically distinct VOCs. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveal that analyte-dependent noncovalent interactions, particularly strong hydrogen bonding in the case of formic acid, underlie the observed selectivity. By integrating energy harvesting and multivariate sensing within a single organic photovoltaic platform, this work establishes a scalable, battery-free approach to artificial olfaction, offering a promising pathway for distributed and long-term VOC monitoring systems.

papers.title: Longitudinal mother-rated screening of male partners' depressive symptoms using the Edinburgh postnatal depression scale during the perinatal period.
papers.abstract: This study examined the validity of a mother-rated partner version of the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS-MRP) for screening perinatal depressive symptoms in male partners and the factors associated with proxy-rating accuracy. A longitudinal survey was conducted with 201 pregnant women (i.e., mothers) and their male partners recruited from three facilities during pregnancy and at 3-6 months postpartum. Mothers evaluated their partners' depressive symptoms using the EPDS-MRP. Mothers and partners completed the Beck Depression Inventory-Second Edition (BDI-II), partners completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), and both completed the Mother-to-Infant Bonding Scale postpartum. Mothers completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Adults (STAI-JYZ). According to the EPDS, 17.4% of male partners had suspected depressive symptoms at each time point. Positive correlations were found between partners' BDI-II and EPDS scores (r = 0.598-0.634, p < .01). Although mothers' EPDS-MRP scores were lower than partners' self-rated EPDS scores at both time points (both ps < 0.001), EPDS-MRP scores correlated positively with partners' BDI-II and EPDS scores (r = 0.229-0.336, p < .01). Lower item-level agreement between self-reports and proxy reports on the EPDS/EPDS-MRP was observed among mothers with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms at both time points (both ps = 0.001), high state anxiety at both time points (p = .022 and p = .041), and high trait anxiety during pregnancy (p = .044). Maternal proxy assessment of male partners' depressive symptoms using the EPDS-MRP may be informative, but proxy-rating accuracy was associated with mothers' mental health symptoms.

papers.title: Driving Sustainability in Medical Technology: Lessons Learned from an Industry Organization's Initiatives.
papers.abstract: GOALS: Environmental sustainability is increasingly recognized as a strategic priority across healthcare due to its implications for population health, organizational resilience, workforce safety, supply chain stability, and long-term healthcare costs. This descriptive medical industry case study describes how a global medical technology organization operationalized sustainability through an enterprise governance model. Specifically, we examine lessons learned from initiatives focused on materials stewardship, alternative sterilization methods, design for sustainability, and circular economy solutions, and identify leadership strategies that may help health systems and industry leaders advance sustainability objectives while maintaining patient safety, quality, operational performance, and healthcare delivery priorities. METHODS: A descriptive case study methodology was used to examine sustainability initiatives implemented through a global medical technology organization's Sustainable Medical Technologies Institute. Program learnings, governance processes, product lifecycle initiatives, and external collaborative projects across four sustainability domains were synthesized to identify implementation approaches, cross-functional operational enablers, and practical lessons relevant to healthcare and industry leaders. PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Successful sustainability integration requires leadership commitment, enterprise governance, and multidisciplinary collaboration rather than isolated environmental initiatives. Key lessons included using morphology-based assessments to prioritize DEHP replacement opportunities, identifying packaging and material constraints that influence adoption of alternative sterilization technologies, establishing value-chain partnerships to evaluate healthcare plastics recycling, and implementing a Design for Sustainability framework to guide lifecycle decision making. papers.title: Combined Sensate Focus and Pelvic Floor Muscle Training versus Pelvic Floor Muscle Training Alone for Sexual Function in Women with Stress Urinary Incontinence: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is the most common subtype of urinary incontinence among women, with reported prevalence ranging from approximately 15% to 35% depending on population and diagnostic criteria, and it impairs sexual function through physiological and psychological mechanisms. Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) addresses anatomical deficits but not psychosocial barriers such as intimacy avoidance and performance anxiety. Sensate focus, a psychobehavioral technique, reduces performance demand and reconnects couples with pleasurable bodily sensations. This trial evaluated whether combining sensate focus with PFMT yields superior improvement in sexual function versus PFMT alone in married women with SUI. METHODS: In this parallel-group, superiority randomized controlled trial across private gynecology clinics in Tehran and Qom, Iran, 60 married women (18-49 years) with clinically confirmed SUI were randomized 1:1 to combined sensate focus plus PFMT (n=30) or PFMT alone (n=30). Primary outcome was FSFI score change at baseline, 1, and 2 months; secondary outcome was pelvic floor muscle (PFM) strength (Modified Oxford Grading Scale). Outcome assessment was not blinded. RESULTS: Total FSFI score rose from 16.97±4.21 to 30.68±0.54 with combined treatment but fell from 20.74±4.74 to 16.53±3.20 with PFMT alone (mean change from baseline +13.7 vs -4.2 points), an adjusted between-group difference in change of 17.8 points (95% CI 16.2-19.5; p<0.001), exceeding the minimum clinically important difference (8-10 points). PFM strength improved more with combined treatment, adjusted difference 1.21 grades (95% CI 0.97-1.46; p<0.001). CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial of 60 women followed for two months, combining sensate focus with PFMT was associated with clinically meaningful improvement in sexual function and PFM strength beyond PFMT alone. papers.title: Burden of depression attributable to intimate partner violence among females aged 15-34 years: global burden of disease study 1990-2021.
papers.journal: International journal of injury control and safety promotion
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major risk factor for depression. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021, we assessed IPV-attributable depression burden among females aged 15-34 years across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. In 2021, the highest age-standardized DALY rates were observed in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, while Low SDI regions had the highest rate (48.85 per 100,000; 95% UI: 0.22-107.47). Globally, DALYs increased from 1.53 million in 1990 to 2.79 million in 2021, whereas the age-standardized DALY rate remained stable (EAPC = -0.08, 95% CI: -0.21 to 0.06). ARIMA and Holt's exponential smoothing models projected a continued increase in absolute DALYs among females through 2050. LMDI analysis identified population growth as the main contributor in Low SDI regions and epidemiological change as the main contributor in High SDI regions. Inequality analysis indicated widening socioeconomic disparities. These findings support targeted IPV prevention, resource allocation, and trauma-informed mental health services for females aged 15-34 years.

papers.title: Intimate partner violence and common mental disorders among women in Mozambique: Evidence from the 2022-2023 Mozambique Demographic and Health Survey.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health concern and a violation of fundamental human right which disproportionately affects women and profoundly impacts mental health. This study used the 2023 Mozambique Demographic and Health Survey data to examine the association between IPV and common mental disorders (CMDs) among 2,790 reproductive-aged women in union. A composite outcome variable (CMDs), from either probable depression or anxiety, was computed using standardised thresholds. The main exposure was IPV, a composite focused on three forms: physical, emotional, and sexual, stratified by never, past, or recent exposures. A weighted binary logistic regression was performed in STATA 18/MP. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals were reported. The results show that the prevalence of probable depression and anxiety was 8.6% (95% CI: 7.1-10.5) and 10.7% (95% CI: 8.7-12.9) respectively. Overall, the prevalence of CMDs was 13.5% (95% CI: 11.4-15.9), comorbid symptoms was 5.8% (95% CI: 4.5 - 7.5). The prevalence of emotional, physical, and sexual IPV was 16.1%, 12.0%, and 4.0% respectively. Women who experienced any recent IPV (aOR = 2.05, 95% CI: 1.36 - 3.09), or past IPV (aOR = 1.40 CI: 0.80 - 2.44) had higher odds of CMDs compared to those who did not experience IPV. After adjusting for confounders, emotional IPV (aOR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.6-3.4) remained independently associated with CMDs; physical (aOR=1.21, 95% CI: 0.73 - 2.03) and sexual IPV (1.67, 95% CI: 0.83 - 3.35) were not. Higher household wealth was protective against CMDs (aOR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.13 - 0.88), and joint household decision-making was associated with higher odds of CMDs (aOR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.08 - 3.15). The results demonstrate an interaction between marital status and IPV on CMDs, providing partial empirical support for Intersectionality theory.
